title: The Salt Road Itinerary
author: Khalavar Tazim sar-Qadrun
pages: From the Sunthrone to the sea is eleven days by camel, fifteen by mule, and forever on foot. Leave at dawn, rest at noon under awnings, and walk again until the sun is a hand above the dunes.
Drink at every Waterhouse even if you are not thirsty. Leave a coin in the cistern bowl even if you are poor. A Waterhouse with no coins is a Waterhouse that will be dry next year.
If the dunes move against the wind, if the wells you knew run dry, if your camels refuse to walk at noon: turn back. Ashkaruun is waking. No cargo is worth being swallowed.
Do not dig in the old sand-streets for Ishkarai gold. Some tombs were sealed facing away from dawn. What comes out of those is dry and angry and does not mind the sun.
At the coast, trade by day with the Tidefolk and they will honour it. Trade by night with the skrell and you will get a better price and no recourse. Choose with your eyes open.
